formula.fn.REPLACE: Replaces a fixed run of characters with new text.

formula.fn.UPPER: Converts the text to upper case.
formula.fn.LOWER: Converts the text to lower case.
formula.fn.TODAY: The current UTC date as a date serial; recalculates on demand.
formula.fn.NOW: The current UTC date and time as a serial; recalculates on demand.
formula.fn.DATE: Builds a date serial from a year, month, and day.

formula.fn.MONTH: The month (1-12) of a date serial.
formula.fn.DAY: The day of the month of a date serial.

formula.fn.MEDIAN: The middle value of the numbers.
formula.fn.STDEV.S: Standard deviation of a sample; needs at least two numbers.

formula.fn.SORT: Sorts rows by one or more columns without changing the source.

dialog.formulaHelp.title: Formula and Function Help
dialog.formulaHelp.intro: Formulas begin with = and are evaluated entirely offline in this page. Search below, or browse the reference.
dialog.formulaHelp.noResults: No help entries match your search.
dialog.formulaHelp.syntaxBody: A formula starts with = followed by an expression, for example =A1+B1*2. Text values use double quotes ("like this"). Whitespace is ignored. Formulas are a spreadsheet (RSF) feature; entering one in a plain CSV offers to convert the document.
dialog.formulaHelp.referencesBody: Refer to a cell by its column letters and 1-based row number. A1 is relative: copying or filling the formula shifts it by the same offset. A $ marker fixes a component when the formula is copied or filled: $A$1 is fully absolute (never shifts), $A1 fixes only the column, and A$1 fixes only the row. For example, filling =A1*$B$1 down one row gives =A2*$B$1. Inserting or deleting rows/columns adjusts absolute and relative references alike, keeping every reference pointing at the same data. $ markers also work as range endpoints, e.g. SUM($A$1:$A10).
dialog.formulaHelp.rangesBody: A rectangular range is two corner references joined by a colon (A1:B10). A:A or A:C covers whole columns; 1:1 or 2:10 covers whole rows. Whole-column and whole-row ranges are bounded to the used grid, never an infinite sheet.
dialog.formulaHelp.operatorsBody: Arithmetic: + - * / with parentheses for grouping. Comparisons = <> < > <= >= return TRUE or FALSE, useful as the condition in IF.
dialog.formulaHelp.errorsIntro: When a formula cannot be evaluated it shows an error code as its value:
dialog.formulaHelp.err.error: The formula is not valid (a syntax error).
dialog.formulaHelp.err.name: An unknown function or name was used.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.value: A value has the wrong type (for example adding text), or a range was used where a single value is required.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.div0: Division by zero (including AVERAGE of no numbers).
dialog.formulaHelp.err.ref: A reference points to a cell that was deleted or is otherwise invalid.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.cycle: A circular reference: a formula depends on its own result, directly or indirectly.
dialog.formulaHelp.autocompleteBody: While typing a function name a suggestion list appears; press Tab or Enter to accept, or Esc to dismiss. While editing a formula, click a cell to insert its reference, or drag across cells to insert a range.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.na: A lookup found no match. XLOOKUP can return a value of your choice instead.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.num: A number is out of range, or a calculation produced no finite result.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.spill: A dynamic array cannot write its result: something is in the way, or it would run past the last row or column.
dialog.formulaHelp.err.calc: A dynamic array produced no values at all, for example FILTER with nothing matching.
dialog.formulaHelp.criteriaBody: A criterion is a value, or text starting with a comparison operator. Text matches case-insensitively. * matches any run of characters and ? matches exactly one; write ~* , ~? , or ~~ for a literal one. An ordering comparison such as ">10" only matches numbers, and "<>x" only matches text; "" matches blank cells and "<>" matches non-blank ones. Every criteria range must have the same shape, otherwise the result is #VALUE!.
dialog.formulaHelp.lookupsBody: XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, and MATCH return #N/A when nothing matches; XLOOKUP's fourth argument replaces that with a value of your choice. XLOOKUP supports exact matching (match_mode 0) and wildcard matching (2), searching forwards (search_mode 1) or backwards (-1); the approximate and binary-search modes are not implemented and report #VALUE! rather than quietly searching a different way. VLOOKUP and MATCH do offer approximate matching, which assumes the lookup column is sorted ascending — with unsorted data the answer is defined but not meaningful.
dialog.formulaHelp.datesBody: A date is a number: serial 0 is 1899-12-30, whole numbers are days, and the fractional part is the time of day. All conversions use UTC, so a workbook computes the same values on every machine and in any timezone. DATE rolls month and day overflow into neighbouring months and years, so DATE(2020, 3, 0) is the last day of February. Dates display as their serial number; use YEAR, MONTH, and DAY to read the parts. TODAY and NOW are volatile: they update when the workbook is edited or when you choose Recalculate, never on a background timer.
dialog.formulaHelp.textBody: LEN, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, and REPLACE count Unicode code points, so Japanese characters and emoji are never cut in half. A combining accent and a multi-person emoji each count as more than one, because the alternative would make results depend on the host's Unicode tables. TRIM removes surrounding whitespace and collapses runs of ordinary spaces, but never touches line breaks or ideographic spaces. Text results are capped at 32,767 characters.
dialog.formulaHelp.arraysBody: FILTER, UNIQUE, SORT, and SEQUENCE return a whole rectangle of values. The formula stays in one cell — the spill anchor — and the rest of the rectangle is filled in automatically. Those filled cells are not editable: edit or clear the anchor instead. If anything is in the way, or the rectangle would run past the last row or column, the anchor shows #SPILL! and writes nothing at all. Only the anchor's formula is saved; the spilled values are recomputed each time the file is opened. Arithmetic does not spread over an array: =SEQUENCE(3)+1 is #VALUE!, not three numbers.
dialog.formulaHelp.section.filterVsFilte: FILTER() is not the Filter command
dialog.formulaHelp.filterVsFilterBody: The FILTER function computes a new list of matching rows into empty cells, leaving the source untouched. The Data > Filter command hides non-matching rows of the sheet you are looking at, changes no values, and is saved with the file. They are independent: filtering a sheet does not change what FILTER returns.

dialog.about.title: About Refrain Sheet
dialog.about.tagline: A local-first, format-preserving CSV and spreadsheet editor.
dialog.about.body: Refrain Sheet edits CSV field values while preserving everything else byte-for-byte where possible: delimiters, quoting, whitespace, line endings, encodings, BOMs, undecodable bytes, and malformed regions. Lightweight spreadsheet editing — formulas, structural edits, and metadata — is available through RSF (Refrain Sheet Format). It runs fully offline; no data ever leaves this page.
dialog.shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
dialog.shortcuts.note: Shortcuts are optional accelerators; every command is also on the menus. They deliberately avoid browser-reserved keys (Ctrl+N/T/W, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+Tab, reload, print, zoom, dev tools).
dialog.shortcuts.appearanceNote: Theme: choose View > Theme (System default, Light, or Dark). System default follows your OS/browser setting and updates live. View > Spreadsheet Zoom scales the spreadsheet area (50–200%) without touching browser zoom — use Zoom In/Out (Ctrl+Shift+. / Ctrl+Shift+,), Reset (Ctrl+Shift+0), or Ctrl/Cmd + mouse wheel over the grid; RSF documents remember their zoom, column widths, and filters. Sheet > Filter hides non-matching rows in RSF documents without changing their data. Language lives under View > Language. While editing a cell or the formula bar, press Alt+Enter to insert a line break within the cell; editing tips appear as tooltips (View > Editing Help Tooltips). Japanese, Chinese, and Korean IME input is fully supported — start typing to begin composition in the cell.

dialog.flashFill.title: Flash Fill
dialog.flashFill.csvOnly: Flash Fill fills many cells at once, which a byte-preserving CSV document never allows. Convert the document to an RSF spreadsheet first (Sheet > Convert to Spreadsheet (RSF)…), then run Flash Fill. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.flashFill.noExamples: Type one or more example results into the target column first (starting at the top of the data), then run Flash Fill on that column. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.flashFill.noSources: No source data was found: the other columns are empty for these rows, so there is nothing to infer a pattern from. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.flashFill.noPattern: No reliable pattern could be inferred from your examples — the supported transformations (copying, joining, splitting, prefixes/suffixes, simple casing) cannot reproduce them exactly. Nothing has been changed. Adjust or add examples and try again.
dialog.flashFill.ambiguous: The examples match more than one different pattern — for example one pattern would produce "{a}" where another would produce "{b}". To avoid an unsafe guess, nothing has been changed. Add another example that tells the patterns apart and try again.
dialog.flashFill.nothing: There is nothing to fill: every remaining cell in the target column already has its inferred value (or there are no rows below the examples). Nothing has been changed.
dialog.flashFill.overwriteWarning: Warning: {n} of these cell(s) are NOT empty and their current values will be overwritten if you apply.
dialog.flashFill.sampleNote: …and {n} more cell(s) not shown in this sample.
dialog.flashFill.note: Applying is a single undoable operation (Ctrl+Z restores every cell). Cancel leaves the document unchanged.
notify.flashFilled: Flash Fill changed {n} cell(s). Undo with Ctrl+Z.

dialog.filter.title: Filter
dialog.filter.csvOnly: Filtering is a spreadsheet feature that hides rows without changing the file's structure, which a byte-preserving CSV document never does. Convert the document to an RSF spreadsheet first (Sheet > Convert to Spreadsheet (RSF)…), then filter. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.filter.noData: No data was found around the active cell to filter. Select the range you want to filter first. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.filter.invalid: The filter could not be applied because its criteria were out of range. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.filter.headerRow: Treat the first row of the range as a header (never hidden)
dialog.filter.headerLocked: The header-row setting and range are fixed while a filter is active. Clear all filters to choose a different range.
dialog.filter.valuesTruncated: This column has many distinct values; only the first are listed. Use a condition above to match values that are not shown.
dialog.filter.combineNote: Within this column, conditions combine using the AND/OR choice above, and the selected values (if restricted) must also match.
dialog.filter.crossNote: Across columns, all column filters must match (AND). {n} other column(s) currently have criteria.
dialog.sort.title: Sort
dialog.sort.csvOnly: Sorting is a spreadsheet feature that reorders how rows display without changing the file's structure, which a byte-preserving CSV document never does. Convert the document to an RSF spreadsheet first (Sheet > Convert to Spreadsheet (RSF)…), then sort. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.sort.noData: No data was found around the active cell to sort. Select the range you want to sort first. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.sort.invalid: The sort could not be applied because its criteria were out of range or invalid (an empty list, too many levels, or the same column used twice). Nothing has been changed.
dialog.sort.headerRow: Treat the first row of the range as a header (never reordered)
dialog.sort.headerLocked: The header-row setting and range are fixed while a sort is active. Clear the sort to choose a different range.
dialog.sort.note: Sorting only changes how rows display: it never saves with the file, never touches cell data or formulas, and is not undoable — clear the sort to restore document order. Combined with an active filter, hidden rows stay in place and only the visible rows are reordered. Editing is disabled inside the sorted range; clear the sort first.
dialog.dataValidation.title: Data Validation
dialog.dataValidation.csvOnly: Data validation is a spreadsheet feature that restricts which values a cell accepts, which a byte-preserving CSV document has no way to store. Convert the document to an RSF spreadsheet first (Sheet > Convert to Spreadsheet (RSF)…), then set a rule. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.dataValidation.invalid: The rule could not be applied because it was out of range or invalid. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.dataValidation.tooMany: This worksheet already has the maximum number of data-validation rules. Clear an existing rule before adding another. Nothing has been changed.
dialog.dataValidation.listHint: Blank lines are ignored; duplicates are removed. A blank cell always stays valid.
dialog.dataValidation.incomplete: Enter at least one allowed value, or a minimum and/or maximum.
dialog.cellComment.title: Cell Comment
dialog.cellComment.csvOnly: Cell comments are a spreadsheet feature that attaches a note to a cell, which a byte-preserving CSV document has no way to store. Convert the document to an RSF spreadsheet first (Sheet > Convert to Spreadsheet (RSF)…), then add a comment. Nothing has been changed.

dialog.convert.title: Convert to Spreadsheet (RSF)?
dialog.convert.formula: You entered a formula. Formulas cannot be stored in "{name}" without giving up the byte-preservation guarantee, so the document must become an RSF spreadsheet document. If you cancel, the text is kept as a plain value.
dialog.convert.paste: This paste does not fit into the existing rows and columns of "{name}". A byte-preserving CSV document never changes its row/column structure silently, so the document must become an RSF spreadsheet document first.
dialog.convert.structure: Inserting or deleting rows or columns changes the structure of "{name}". A byte-preserving CSV document never changes its structure, so the document must become an RSF spreadsheet document first.
dialog.convert.fill: Filling copies values and formulas across multiple cells of "{name}", a spreadsheet-only operation. A byte-preserving CSV document is never modified this way, so the document must become an RSF spreadsheet document first.
dialog.convert.command: Convert "{name}" to an RSF spreadsheet document. RSF supports formulas, row and column insertion and deletion, range fill, persistent column widths, and spreadsheet metadata. The current (including unsaved) contents of "{name}" are used.
dialog.convert.note: After conversion the tab becomes an .rsf spreadsheet document: formulas and row/column edits are supported, but the byte-level preservation guarantee no longer applies and saving produces an .rsf file. The original CSV file on disk is never modified by the conversion. This tab's undo history is cleared.
dialog.convert.commandNote: The converted spreadsheet opens in a new tab; the original CSV tab and the file on disk stay open and unchanged. Conversion ends the byte-identical CSV round-trip guarantee for the new RSF document, which is saved as an .rsf file.
dialog.rsfSave.title: Saved as RSF
dialog.rsfSave.message: "{name}" is a spreadsheet document (formulas, row/column edits, or spreadsheet metadata). CSV cannot store these without losing the original-file guarantees, so it is saved in the .rsf format — a documented, versioned binary format.
dialog.rsfSave.note: To get a plain CSV file with the calculated values instead, use File > Export as CSV…
dialog.exportCsv.title: Export as CSV (lossy)
dialog.exportCsv.message: "{name}" will be exported as a plain CSV file. CSV export is a lossy conversion from an RSF spreadsheet document.
dialog.exportCsv.warning: Formulas are exported as their calculated display values, not as formula expressions. The .rsf document stays open and unchanged.
dialog.exportCsv.notPreserved: Not preserved in the CSV: formulas and their dependency information, row/column structure beyond the exported grid, column widths, document metadata, font preferences, and other spreadsheet-only data.
dialog.exportCsv.bomNote: A byte order mark applies only to UTF-8; the BOM choice is disabled and ignored for Shift_JIS and EUC-JP.
dialog.exportXlsx.title: Export as XLSX (lossy)
dialog.exportXlsx.message: "{name}" will be exported as an .xlsx (Excel Open XML) file.
dialog.exportXlsx.warning: Formulas are exported as their calculated display values, not as formula expressions. The source document stays open and unchanged.
dialog.exportXlsx.notPreserved: Not preserved in the .xlsx: formulas and their dependency information, cell styling and number formats, column widths, filters, and other spreadsheet-only data. Every worksheet is included.
dialog.insertCells.title: Insert Copied Cells
dialog.insertCells.message: Insert the copied {rows} × {cols} cell range at the selection by shifting existing cells.
dialog.insertCells.note: Shifting cells down inserts whole rows across the sheet; shifting cells right inserts whole columns. This keeps every formula consistent: existing references adjust exactly like Insert Rows/Columns, and relative references in the inserted formulas shift by their offset from the copied location. The insertion is a single undoable operation.

dialog.sqlQuery.title: SQL Query
dialog.sqlQuery.intro: Run a read-only SQL query against one worksheet or the open CSV. Nothing here changes the source data — this only reads it.
dialog.sqlQuery.help.body: A single read-only SELECT statement: WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, common comparison and logical operators, BETWEEN/IN/LIKE/IS NULL, and the LOWER/UPPER/TRIM/LENGTH/ABS/ROUND/COALESCE functions. The picked data source is always named "data". INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and other statements that could change data are not allowed.
